entries.name: Commander G
entries.look: Commander G leads the Swiftsoul Chapter of the Iron Fists Guild with ruthless efficiency and a network of contacts that spans both Kingdom officials and underworld figures. She plays all sides, maintains plausible deniability, and runs operations that blur the line between mercenary work and organized crime. She is also the mother of 'X.O.,' whose volatile personality and theatrical demands have apparently injected chaos into Guild decision-making, possibly explaining the messy Swiftsoul operation and the use of Archie Miser as a scapegoat. entries.name: Kyle Coinsoul
entries.look: Kyle Coinsoul is an Iron Fists Guild operative who interacted with Archie Miser shortly before the Swiftsoul explosion. He was seen using an unauthorized override key near Platform 3 and has documented gambling debts that could provide motive for complicity in Guild operations. He is a potential weak link in the Guild's involvement—someone who might flip under pressure if his debts or legal exposure make cooperation attractive. entries.name: P.S
entries.look: X.O. is Commander G's daughter and a destabilizing influence within the Iron Fists Guild's Swiftsoul Chapter. She exhibits profound narcissistic entitlement, a god complex that would embarrass actual deities, and a tendency to view Guild operations as theatrical performances staged for her personal amusement. Her demands for dramatic, often cruel, operational protocols may be responsible for the chaotic nature of the Swiftsoul incident—including the elaborate framing of Archie Miser. entries.name: Parson Pellinost
entries.look: Parson Pellinost is a 'doctor' for the Mages' Guild who perfectly illustrates the Guild's approach to charity. He bypassed heavy magical wards to enter a barricaded room, healed an injured Archie Miser, informed him he was now in debt, and when Archie demanded a refund, Pellinost forcibly ripped the healing magic back out of Archie's body. Waluigi finds the sheer, unadulterated pettiness of this act to be a breathtaking display of aggressive capitalism. WAH. To understand Parson Pellinost is to understand the Mages' Guild. entries.name: Pierce Anamatar
entries.look: A man with knights, a den, and a price list. Pierce Anamatar has appeared twice now in the same role: somebody cornered meets him, and he offers passage in exchange for a possession. On a Shadow Estate rooftop he took a contract to kill the Oracle in exchange for sending the party home. In the burning Skittering Grove he asked for the siglet, settled for a fourteen-year-old's student ID, and called it durable. He does not want coin. He wants things that belong to people. entries.name: The Koopa Prisoner
entries.look: The prisoner nobody in Peach's Castle would describe to a guard. A Koopa in an unlocked cell, expecting a friend at the door and getting a ceremonial guard with a lantern — *so you finally came to free me — oh. It's you.* He shook Fawful's hand in front of three Mages' Guild hoods, reached Fawful's bean shop before the Toad who crawled five hours through the drains to find it, and admitted there that he had led the escort into the ambush and had himself alerted the castle to Bowser's attack. entries.name: Valorian Stormweave
entries.look: Valorian Stormweave was a Senior Enforcer of the Mages' Guild who—according to Lady Bloomia's testimony—was present at the Royal Vault on the morning of Princess Peach's assassination in 955 BF. He allegedly delayed the Solstice Crown delivery, knew Bloomia's name without introduction, smiled 'like a predator who has confirmed the location of its prey,' and was part of the Guild's involvement in 'the arrangement.'
